title: Donchian ensemble: majority vote of four daily channels, no stop
ex_ante_rule: Protocol docs/protocolo-validacao-v3.md section 2.2. Signals come from CLOSED daily candles (merge_informative_pair, ffill, as in Sma200Baseline) and are executed on the 1h chart at the next open. Four members (N, M) = (20,10), (55,20), (100,50), (200,100). Member state is a two-level latch computed on the daily frame: ON when daily close > max(daily high of the N days before the current day) ; OFF when daily close < min(daily low of the M days before the current day) ; otherwise the previous state is kept ; undefined (NaN) channel values give OFF. Channels use rolling(N).max().shift(1) and rolling(M).min().shift(1) on the daily frame before the merge. ENTRY: at least 2 of the 4 members are ON and the strategy is flat (level entry, including the first candle of a split if already ON). EXIT: fewer than 2 members ON. No stop-loss (stoploss attribute -0.99 only to satisfy the engine contract), no take-profit, no sizing hooks, no cooldown. Exposure is the fixed share chosen by the lab rule (bootstrap.choose_exposure on exploration trades). Sensitivities reported, never selectable: threshold 1 and 3 of 4, each member alone, the vote without member (20,10), thresholds counted in the DSR N. Warm-up: 400 bars (daily candles; the state at the first day of a split was verified equal to the full-history state for 400, 600 and 900 days on BTC, ETH and BNB).
rationale: Mechanism: trend-following profits from slow reaction to information and from the persistence of large moves (time-series momentum). A single Donchian lookback is the main source of overfitting in channel rules; voting across four fixed horizons removes the choice of one lookback and is how the cited crypto study combines channel models. Expected trades: roughly 10 to 30 per pair in the exploration window; the minimum of 30 trades per pair may not be met (protocol D-2 keeps the gate, so an inconclusive result is possible and is reported as such). Round trip cost 0.35 percent at base is small against multi-week moves, but the member (20,10) trades most and is the most cost sensitive. This is NOT volatility sizing: that is a non-decisive overlay in the protocol. Honest caveat: the family was chosen after seeing that trend rules worked in this history, and the cited study could not be read in full here.
novelty_vs_tried: H-002 was a single 20/10 channel on 1h bars with a 10 percent stop (rejected: drawdown 60 to 98 percent). H-007, H-009 and H-017 are 1h breakout rules with a regime gate. This rule works on daily channels, four horizons, a majority vote and no stop; it is the closest relative of Sma200Baseline at the long members, so redundancy with it is expected and will be measured.
